title: JSON to TOON Converter – Use Fewer Tokens | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert JSON to TOON and TOON back to JSON in your browser, and see how many tokens it saves before you paste data into an AI chat. Free, no upload.
heading: JSON to TOON
subtitle: Rewrite JSON as compact TOON to save tokens in an AI chat, or turn TOON back into JSON.
intro: TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) is an open format that writes the same data as JSON with fewer tokens. It saves the most on lists of objects with the same keys: instead of repeating every key for every item, TOON writes one header line with the field names and then one row per item. Paste JSON or open a .json file to get TOON before you paste the data into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, or paste TOON to get JSON back. The token count before and after, and the saving in percent, are shown beside the result. The conversion runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded or sent to any AI service.

faq.question: Is my text uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The JSON or TOON you paste stays in this tab and is converted by your own browser; it is never sent to a server or to any AI service. Nothing is saved on the site: no share links and no history.

faq.question: What is TOON?
faq.answer: Token-Oriented Object Notation, an open format for the same data as JSON with less repetition. A list of objects with the same keys becomes one header line with the field names, then one row of values per item, so the keys are written once instead of for every item.

faq.question: How much does TOON save?
faq.answer: It depends on the data. Long lists of records with the same keys often save a large share of the tokens; deeply nested or irregular data saves little, sometimes nothing. The page shows the counts before and after, so you can see the real saving for your data.

faq.question: Will an AI chat understand TOON?
faq.answer: TOON is new, and not every tool reads it. When you paste it into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, say that the data is in TOON format; the header line with the field names makes it easy to follow.

faq.question: Can I turn TOON back into JSON?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose TOON to JSON, paste the TOON and copy the JSON or download it as a .json file.

faq.question: What if my JSON has a mistake?
faq.answer: The converter shows the error instead of a result. The JSON viewer points to the line with the problem so you can fix it.

faq.question: Can I hide names and emails in the data first?
faq.answer: Yes. Mask data hides names, emails, phone numbers and IDs in CSV, Excel, JSON and text files, so you can mask the JSON before converting it.

faq.question: How do I convert JSON to TOON?
faq.answer: Paste the JSON into OpenAnyDoc's JSON to TOON converter, choose JSON to TOON, and copy the result or download a .toon file; the token count before and after is shown. The conversion runs in your browser, so the data is not uploaded.
